messages:
pagerduty-bot: SEV2 — high-error-rate detected for ingress fanout (eastus2 AZ-b). 5xx surge starting ~10:42 UTC affecting api-gateway and inference-proxy. Pager: @oncall-emma, escalation path: SRE team.
oncall-emma: acknowledged. jumping in. seeing 5xx spikes & Envoy upstream 502s on multiple clusters. can others confirm? :rotating_light:
sre-erin: I see repeated connreset and 502 traces in envoy logs, mostly workers talking to NLB backends in az-b. Error pattern: TCP RST mid-handshake -> upstream unhealthy. Graphs: 5xx -> 12% of global requests peaked, eastus2 AZ-b ~80% of those.
infra-ben: checking cloud health pages — no full region outage but provider notes "network fabric event" in eastus2-b ongoing. opening support case with provider now.
runtime-alex: quick check: ALB target groups in AZ-b show target health flipping to unhealthy on 30s interval. NLB connection counts also jump. Might be asymmetric egress or path issues causing keepalive resets.
oncall-emma: immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop new session distribution to AZ-b (drain targets) 2) shift traffic away with weighted DNS to other AZs/regions for critical routes 3) enable extra retries+timeouts for inference-proxy calls. @infra-ben can you start the target drain? @runtime-alex please prepare retry toggle.
infra-ben: initiating target drain for alb/ingress in eastus2-b now. command: ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn <arn> --targets Id=i-xxxx``` will iterate. doing gradual drain (30s between steps).
runtime-alex: deploying hotfix toggle: increase upstream retries to 3 and backoff to 200ms for inference-proxy. patch applied to canary pods in eastus2-a and euc1. manifest snippet: ```env: - name: PROXY_RETRIES value: "3" - name: PROXY_BACKOFF_MS value: "200"```
product-liz: heads-up to product & comms — which customer segments impacted? CS, please prioritize top accounts.
cs-maya: checking error reports from support. Initial look: several corporate customers hitting higher latency + 5xx during the window, some API keys saw elevated errors. Estimating 8-12% of active customers saw degraded requests for 10-20 minutes. I'll flag top 10 customers to AMs.
sre-erin: after drain started, connection resets dropped ~50% in 2m, 5xx dropped to ~4% overall. still elevated vs baseline. DNS shift next: weighted host-level routing to send 80% of traffic to eastus2-a + remote region euc1 for critical routes.
infra-ben: executing weighted DNS change via Route53: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZ --change-batch file://shift.json``` using TTL 30s. pushing 80/20 split across AZs and fallback to euc1 for specific endpoint prefixes.
oncall-emma: monitoring. please post any deploy/link commands you run.
support-bot: Automated notification: Incident page created — https://internal.incidents/2976543210. Pager duty case ID PD-83421.
runtime-alex: canary results look good, 5xx for canary routes is back to baseline. scaling healthy AZs + removing AZ-b from rotation should carry load.
sre-erin: I still see a small number of apps hitting NLB-level TCP RSTs for long-lived connections (keepalives). proposing to reduce keepalive timeout on envoy -> backend to force reconnects quicker, and enable connection-level backoff in NLB configuration where possible.
infra-ben: changed ALB/NLB deregistration in batches completed. provider support confirmed a "fabric polymerization" (their term) causing transient path blackholes to a subset of AZ-b hosts. They say their mitigation is rolling and should stabilize in 20-30min.
product-liz: compiling impact statement for sales & status page. ETA for preliminary customer note?
cs-maya: draft message ready. will send to top customers and ops channel now. short note: "We experienced increased 5xx in eastus2 due to cloud networking instability. Traffic shifted and service restored; we continue to monitor."
oncall-emma: handing off to @sre-erin for ongoing monitoring and RCA. My shift ends in 40m — I set the incident status to monitoring and added runbook steps followed.
sre-erin: taking over incident lead. moving to postmitigation checklist: 1) confirm provider fully restored 2) monitor 1hr at normal load 3) collect envoy + ALB/NLB logs for trending 4) schedule postmortem meeting.
infra-ben: provider updated support case: fabric repairs progressing; recommend us to keep degraded AZ-b drained for 1 hour to ensure no resurface.
runtime-alex: creating temporary runtime mitigation: add circuit-breaker for long-lived connections to NLB backends to prevent cascading resets. config snippet applied: ```circuit_breaker: max_connections: 10000 half_open_ratio: 0.1```
sre-erin: metric summary (peak): 5xx peaked at 12% global, estimated customer impact window ~15 minutes, latency spike + retry amplification accounted for most extra errors. Mitigation reduced 5xx to <1% within 10 minutes.
product-liz: filing incident severity and notifying on-call execs. please assign severity tag in incident tracker.
sre-erin: assigned SEV2. Scheduling postmortem invite for 48h. owners: infra-ben (cloud escalation), runtime-alex (ingress/runtime fix), sre-erin (postmortem writeup).
oncall-emma: thank you team. leaving note: everything stable from my side. :wave:
support-bot: Customer-facing status page updated: "Degraded — partial recovery in progress"; will update to "Operational" once metrics stable for 30m.
sre-erin: final check at +45m: metrics stable, provider says fabric repairs complete. we'll keep AZ-b out of rotation for 60 more minutes as a precaution. logging artifacts uploaded to incident page. closing channel for active paging; follow-up thread will be postmortem writeup.
cs-maya: sent customer notes to top accounts and posted summary to #customer-status. no escalations to execs so far.
infra-ben: follow-up action items created: - add automated failover to regional host-level routing for ingress (reduce TTLs, faster weight changes) - review NLB keepalive settings with provider - test drain automation in staging.
sre-erin: thanks everyone. quick retrospective notes: provider network path instability caused asymmetric resets; our mitigations (drain + weighted DNS + retries + circuit breaker) worked. Postmortem will include timeline, root cause hypothesis, and recommended infra/runtime changes. closing the incident thread.
